text: Louise and Ann went to the movies last night.  They met Charlie there.  Afterwards they all went for a chocolate sundae, but the ice cream parlor was closed.
section: 3.2 A Night on the Town (analysis pp. 47-53; template text base pp. 53-54)
notes: Template text base has numbered propositions 1-17 (P18-P20 are printed as null placeholders) with inferred propositions marked '>': 1.(CONJ: AND, LOUISE, ANN); 2.(GO, A:1, G:MOVIES); 3.(QUALIFY, NIGHT, LAST); 4.(TIME: >DURING, 2, 3); 5.(MEET, A:1, O:CHARLIE); 6.(LOC: AT, 5, MOVIES); 7.(CONJ: AND, LOUISE, ANN, CHARLIE); 8.(GO, A:7, >S:MOVIES, >G:12); 9.(QUALITY OF, SUNDAE, CHOCOLATE); >10.(GET, A:7, O:9); 11.(PURP: FOR, 8, >10); 12.(QUALIFY, PARLOR, ICE CREAM); 13.(CLOSE, A:$, O:12); >14.(NEGATE, >10); >15.(CAUS: BECAUSE, 13, >14); 16.(CONC: BUT, 11, >14); 17.(TIME: AFTERWARDS, 5, 11). Because the temporal reference of 'afterwards' is ambiguous, two alternative endings are also listed: branch a (>17a.(END, A:MOVIES); 18a.(TIME: AFTERWARDS, >17a, 11)) and branch b (>17b.(END, A:MOVIES); 18b.(TIME: AFTERWARDS, 5, 11); 19b.(TIME: AFTERWARDS, 11, >17b); 20b.(CONJ: ALSO, 18b, 19b)). A footnote on p. 49 notes two additional implied reference propositions >A.(REF, THEY, 1) and >B.(REF, THERE, MOVIES) that are ignored in the base. Counting only the core list, 17 propositions; 23 distinct non-null propositions including both alternative branches.

text: Three fourths of Australia's sheep are pure Merinos.  They are popular because of the large amount of semiarid land.  The Merino thrives on the grasses and low bushes which grow on semiarid plains.  They are known for their heavy fleeces of fine-quality wool which bring a high price from textile manufacturers.
